correctness.rationale: The exact POEM-ES v2 Algorithm 1 uses r-scaled symmetric finite differences and Sigma^(-1/2) transformed normalized sphere directions, with first step eta0=1/||g0|| for r_epsilon=1. For f(x)=a·x on a radius-two disk, g0=2(a·Sigma^{1/2}v)Sigma^{-1/2}v and projection is inactive, hence the expected decrease is the signed angular integral in the package. The arcsinh and arcsin primitives reproduce the exact finite-delta formula including coordinate axes. Its minimizers are trapped at q between constants/sqrt(log(1/delta)) by positive-term bounds and a matching trial direction; uniform rescaling q=t/sqrt(L) gives limiting cost t/2+1/t and unique t=sqrt2, yielding m_delta~(2sqrt2/pi)sqrt(delta L). Independently evaluated the exact formula against direct 2pi-angle numerical quadrature at five pairs and checked decreasing-delta minimizers; these tests do not replace the uniform asymptotic argument.

value.rationale: The normalized single-step progress under anisotropic zeroth-order sampling is a natural algorithmic invariant: this exact minimax quantifies a genuine loss and identifies a counterintuitive moving worst-slope direction with sharp logarithmic correction. The analysis does not claim later-iteration rate or paper-sized algorithmic improvement, but the precise worst-angle diagnostic can guide understanding of preconditioner conditioning.

limitations: Applies only to normalized first step of exact v2 POEM-ES, two dimensions, linear 1-Lipschitz objectives, fixed covariance, no noise and no active projection.
No multistep or convergence-optimality claim and no claim that anisotropic sensitivity itself is new.
